append.note: runs an additional subsearch; repeated appends re-scan the base data

dedup.note: streaming only in limited no-sortby cases; prefer stats latest()/values()

delete.note: destructive — always blocked in guarded execution

eventstats.note: holds whole result set in memory on SH

fillnull.note: dataset_processing when no field list is given (must inspect all events for fields)

join.note: SH-only; right side is a subsearch bound by subsearch_maxout_join (50k) and 60s — silent truncation risk

localop.note: forces remainder of pipeline onto the SH

lookup.note: distributable only when the lookup bundle replicates; huge lookups degrade

map.note: spawns one search per input row up to maxsearches — concurrency storm risk

noop.note: carries directives, e.g. search_optimization=false for optimizer A/B

rex.note: greedy patterns on _raw are CPU-heavy even though distributable

search.note: generating when first in the pipeline

sort.note: buffers full input; sort immediately before transaction is a smell

table.note: drops fields and centralizes — end-of-pipeline only; use fields to trim mid-pipeline

transaction.note: memory-bound on SH; maxopentxn/maxopenevents LRU eviction silently drops events; requires descending time order; >90% of uses are better served by stats

tstats.note: also usable mid-pipeline (append=t); still needs index/sourcetype scoping under DMA

union.note: prefer over repeated append; can stream when all branches are streaming

command_types.description: SPL command classification for the deterministic critique tier. Types drive pipeline-order checks (e.g. centralized-before-filter). Aligned with Splunk Search Reference 'Commands by type' and knowledge/spl-map-reduce-and-command-types.md.

types.centralized_streaming: Streaming but must run on the search head in event order. Creates a map-reduce barrier; never place before narrow filters.
types.dataset_processing: Requires the whole dataset before acting (sort-like buffering) but is not stats-shaped.
types.distributable_streaming: Operates on each event independently; runs on indexers in parallel. Safe (and preferred) early in the pipeline.
types.generating: Fetches events/results; only valid as the first command (or after |). Runs on indexers or SH depending on command.
types.orchestrating: Controls how the search executes (subsearches, joins, appends, optimizer directives). Frequent source of hidden cost.
types.transforming: Requires the full input set to produce output rows (stats-like). Runs on the search head; place after filtering.

limits.description: Platform magic numbers the critique tiers cite. Values are Splunk Enterprise defaults (limits.conf) — environments may differ; deep analysis should read effective values via REST when available.

bands.action: add indexed filters, TERM(), narrow time range
missing index / sourcetype / indexed field filter

efficiency_bands.description: eventCount/scanCount bands used to grade filtering quality when Job Inspector data is available

map_maxsearches.failure_mode: raising it multiplies concurrent search load

max_mem_usage_mb.failure_mode: command output silently limited when the cap is hit
max_mem_usage_mb.source: limits.conf [default] max_mem_usage_mb (per-command memory cap, e.g. mvexpand, eventstats)

maxopenevents.failure_mode: LRU eviction of events inside open transactions

maxopentxn.failure_mode: LRU eviction of open transactions — silently incomplete results

maxresultrows.failure_mode: result sets past the cap are truncated

scheduler_skip_ratio_alert.failure_mode: skip ratio above 20% in 24h warrants investigation

subsearch_maxout.failure_mode: silent truncation — subsearch results beyond the cap are dropped without error

subsearch_maxout_join.failure_mode: canonical log message: '50000 results, truncating to maxout'

subsearch_maxtime.failure_mode: subsearch finalized early — partial input to the outer search

rules.canonical_rewrite: Bound the window (earliest=-24h or the schedule interval); for historical baselines use summary indexing or accelerated data models.
rules.cost_rationale: All-time scheduled searches rescan the entire retention window every run — the canonical scheduled-search resource drain called out in Splunk docs.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: runDuration and scanCount grow monotonically over the search's lifetime
rules.name: All-time search window
rules.risk_rationale: Cost grows without bound as data ages in; Cloud admission rules may hard-block, breaking the workflow that depends on the search.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Join on an explicit key instead of position: one base search with `stats ... BY key`, or a `lookup`. Reserve appendcols for genuinely positional, equal-length, identically-ordered sets.
rules.cost_rationale: appendcols runs its argument as a subsearch (the 50k/60s caps apply) and stitches the columns onto the main results — another indexer round-trip on top of the base search.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: row counts differ between the main search and the appendcols subsearch
rules.name: appendcols joins by row position
rules.risk_rationale: appendcols matches by ROW POSITION, not a key. If the two result sets are ordered differently or have different lengths, every value lands on the wrong row — the output is confidently wrong with no error.

rules.canonical_rewrite: One base search with OR'd scopes plus stats/eval to separate the branches; union when branches are genuinely different datasets.
rules.cost_rationale: Each | append [search ...] dispatches another full search — typically re-scanning the same indexes the base search already read.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: N dispatched subsearches in search.log for one logical question
rules.name: Repeated append subsearches
rules.risk_rationale: Each append is also a subsearch with the 10k/60s caps and their silent truncation behavior.

rules.canonical_rewrite: (index=a cond1) OR (index=a cond2) | stats count(eval(cond1)) AS c1 count(eval(cond2)) AS c2 — or union for genuinely distinct datasets.
rules.cost_rationale: Appending searches that differ only in a filter re-runs retrieval N times. One base search with OR'd scope plus conditional aggregation (stats count(eval(...))) reads the data once.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: single dispatch replaces N in search.log after rewrite
rules.name: append chain where one base search serves
rules.risk_rationale: Inherits subsearch caps per appended branch.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Anchor with index, sourcetype, and at least one indexed term before any wildcard.
rules.cost_rationale: A bare * retrieves everything the platform allows — no lexicon terms to intersect, no bloom filter elimination.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scanCount approaches total events in the time window
rules.name: Bare * retrieval
rules.risk_rationale: Result volume is bounded only by platform limits, so behavior degrades unpredictably as data grows.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Emitted alongside a detector code; the suggested_spl field carries the concrete rewrite.
rules.cost_rationale: Remediation umbrella used in critique output when a rewrite exists: stats by common key, lookup for reference data, single base search with OR plus stats, accelerated data model via tstats.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: A/B runDuration between original and rewrite
rules.name: Cheaper equivalent exists
rules.risk_rationale: Advisory only — carries the rewrite suggestion, not a finding of its own.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Match the window to the question; for scheduled searches, size earliest to the schedule interval plus a safety margin.
rules.cost_rationale: I/O scales linearly with the time window. A -30d window when -24h answers the question is a 30x multiplier on every downstream cost.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: runDuration scales with window; scanCount spread across many buckets
rules.name: Broader time range than needed
rules.risk_rationale: Long windows on scheduled searches push runDuration toward the cron interval — the self-overlap skip pattern.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Drive collect from a single, non-overlapping scheduled search; never backfill by re-running it ad hoc over a window already summarized. Prefer data-model acceleration where it fits.
rules.cost_rationale: collect writes results into a summary index — legitimate for scheduled summary indexing, but it has no dedup intelligence.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: duplicate rows in the target summary index for the same source _time
rules.name: collect duplicates the summary index on re-run
rules.risk_rationale: Re-running collect over a source/time range it already summarized duplicates every row (community reports of >100x inflation), and it uses the original _time so duplicates scatter historically — every downstream report built on the summary is silently inflated. Safe only when scheduled once per non-overlapping window.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Anchor patterns, replace .* with bounded or negated classes ([^"]*), and extract once into fields rather than re-matching.
rules.cost_rationale: Multiple .* in one pattern forces backtracking across full _raw for every event — CPU cost that distributable placement cannot hide.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.rex phase time disproportionate to event volume
rules.name: Greedy regex over _raw
rules.risk_rationale: Pathological backtracking can dominate a search's CPU on hostile input.

rules.canonical_rewrite: | stats latest(status) AS status latest(_time) AS _time BY host — instead of | dedup host.
rules.cost_rationale: dedup keeps arbitrary representatives unless paired with sortby (its non-streaming, expensive mode). stats latest()/values() by key states the intent and aggregates distributably where possible.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: dedup phase cost; result instability across runs
rules.name: dedup where stats latest()/values() serves
rules.risk_rationale: Without sortby, WHICH event survives dedup is order-dependent — subtly nondeterministic results.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Do not delete from a scheduled or ad-hoc search. To remove data use index retention (frozenTimePeriodInSecs) or `splunk clean` on a rebuildable index; to hide a subset, fix the upstream filter — never delete.
rules.cost_rationale: delete marks events unsearchable across the whole environment; it does NOT reclaim disk — the data stays on disk, just hidden from every search.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: delete operations in the _audit index; events vanish from search with disk usage unchanged
rules.name: delete is irreversible and frees no disk
rules.risk_rationale: Irreversible: recovery means re-indexing the source. A too-broad base search silently masks huge swaths of data from all users. A flagged risky command gated behind the can_delete role — its presence in a saved search warrants review every single time.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Use earliest/latest with relative units and snapping: daysago=7 becomes earliest=-7d@d latest=now; searchtimespanhours=1 becomes a matched earliest/latest pair.
rules.cost_rationale: Legacy modifiers (daysago=, startminutesago=, searchtimespanhours=, starttimeu=) are documented as valid but slated for removal, and each is a slower, less flexible path than the relative-time syntax.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: deprecation notices in search.log; the same window expressed two ways
rules.name: Deprecated time modifier
rules.risk_rationale: Removal risk: a future release drops them and the saved search silently breaks. Correctness-adjacent — they express windows less precisely than snap-aware earliest/latest.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Move every distributable filter (search terms, where, fields) ahead of the first centralized command; often the centralized command itself can become stats.
rules.cost_rationale: Centralized streaming commands (transaction, head, streamstats) force all events matched so far onto the search head. Placed before narrow filters, the SH holds an unscoped event set — the map-reduce model inverted.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: high dispatch.stream.remote (bytes shipped to SH) relative to resultCount
rules.name: Centralized command before filtering
rules.risk_rationale: Search head memory pressure affects every user on the SH, not just the offending search.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Reduce the set before the windowed stat (filter early, `fields` down), or use `stats` (which spills to disk) when a global aggregate — not a per-event running value — is what you actually need.
rules.cost_rationale: Both buffer aggregation state on the search head across the whole result set — centralized, not distributable to the indexers.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: computed eventstats/streamstats field absent on a fraction of rows
rules.name: eventstats/streamstats drop columns at the memory cap
rules.risk_rationale: At max_mem_usage_mb (default 200 MB for these) the processor STOPS adding the computed fields to results rather than spilling to disk the way stats does — the column silently goes missing on large sets.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Express what you DO want: enumerate the included values, or filter after retrieval with | where when exclusion is genuinely needed.
rules.cost_rationale: Exclusion (NOT field=x, field!=x) cannot use the lexicon the way inclusion can — Splunk still retrieves candidates and discards them.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scanCount well above what the inclusion form scans
rules.name: Exclusion filter in base search
rules.risk_rationale: != also drops events where the field is absent, which is frequently not what the author intended.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Filter on indexed fields first; trim with fields; consider indexed extractions for hot sourcetypes.
rules.cost_rationale: High command.search.kv means the search pays per-event extraction cost (KV_MODE, search-time props) across the scanned set — often alongside missing early filters.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.search.kv dominates phase timings
rules.name: Heavy search-time field extraction
rules.risk_rationale: Cost signal only.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Scope the search so fewer events flow through enrichment; disable unneeded automatic lookups; enrich after aggregation where possible.
rules.cost_rationale: High command.search.lookups means automatic lookups are applied to every event scanned — large lookup files multiply the effect.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.search.lookups dominates phase timings
rules.name: Heavy automatic lookup enrichment
rules.risk_rationale: Cost signal only.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Constrain eventtype definitions; avoid tag= filters over broad scopes; filter on indexed terms first.
rules.cost_rationale: High command.search.typer means eventtype and tag evaluation is applied per event — environments with many broad eventtypes pay this on every search that touches them.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.search.typer dominates phase timings
rules.name: Heavy eventtype/tag annotation
rules.risk_rationale: Cost signal only.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Aggregate by the dimension you actually report on; bucket continuous values first (bin); use estdc() for distinct counts.
rules.cost_rationale: stats ... by a near-unique field builds one bucket per event — SH memory scales with cardinality and renders crawl.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: stats phase memory; result rows near input events
rules.name: Aggregation by ultra-high-cardinality field
rules.risk_rationale: Commands capped by max_mem_usage_mb silently limit output when the bucket table exceeds the cap.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Widen to */5 or more; if near-real-time latency is a hard requirement, consider an accelerated data model or streaming-style detection instead.
rules.cost_rationale: A */1 cron occupies a scheduler slot 1,440 times a day; few detections genuinely need sub-5-minute latency, and dense schedules crowd out every other search on the host.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scheduler concurrency and skip events while active
rules.name: Every-minute schedule
rules.risk_rationale: Any runtime hiccup immediately self-overlaps; skip storms follow.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Restructure as a single pass: (index=a) OR (index=b) | stats values(...) by join_key — or use lookup for reference data.
rules.cost_rationale: join is SH-only and runs its right side as a subsearch — capped at 50k rows (subsearch_maxout join context) and 60s (subsearch_maxtime). SQL habits port badly: Splunk joins buffer and match on the search head.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: subsearch finalization messages in search.log; right-side result count at exactly the cap
rules.name: join with unbounded subsearch
rules.risk_rationale: Past the caps Splunk truncates silently — the canonical log line is "50000 results, truncating to maxout". The join completes, the answer is wrong, nobody is told.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Move each predicate to the earliest stage where its fields exist; only predicates on derived fields stay after the eval that derives them.
rules.cost_rationale: A search/where predicate that only references fields available earlier could have dropped rows before they were transformed or shipped to the SH. The canonical example: | lookup | eval | search A=25 L>100 — A=25 belongs in the base search, L>100 right after the lookup.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: optimizer A/B (search_optimization=false) shows pushdown gain; residual gap is the movable predicate
rules.name: Movable filter placed late in the pipeline
rules.risk_rationale: Low correctness risk; wasted compute and latency.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Anchor the term: status=fail* instead of *fail*; exact terms or TERM() for tokens; lookup/inputlookup for large ID sets.
rules.cost_rationale: Leading wildcards (*fail, field=*value) bypass the tsidx lexicon AND bloom filters — every term in every bucket must be examined. Trailing wildcards (fail*) can still enumerate the lexicon.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: huge scanCount with tiny resultCount (efficiency band poor/critical)
rules.name: Leading wildcard
rules.risk_rationale: Forces the search from dense toward super-sparse on the density spectrum; a single leading-wildcard search can dominate indexer I/O.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Move the lookup after the transforming command when its output is not part of the group-by or aggregation: ... | stats count by <key> | lookup ... <key> OUTPUT <fields>.
rules.cost_rationale: A lookup runs per event on every row that reaches it. When its output fields are not used by the following transforming command, the enrichment could run AFTER the aggregation — matching a handful of grouped rows instead of every raw event.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.search.lookups events count equals raw input, not grouped rows
rules.name: lookup enrichment before aggregation
rules.risk_rationale: Cost only. Splunk's own lookup docs give the canonical example: ... | stats count by status | lookup status_desc status OUTPUT description beats doing the lookup before the stats.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Expand the search to audit it fully — Search preview (Cmd/Ctrl-Shift-E) or `splunk btool macros list` — then re-run the critique on the expanded SPL.
rules.cost_rationale: Macros expand before the search runs; SPL Critic analyzes the TEXT, so it cannot see inside a `macro` call. A macro can hide any anti-pattern — index=*, all-time, leading wildcards, join, or summariesonly=false (the ES security_content_summariesonly case expands to raw-data scans through two layers of macro).
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: the expanded search string in Job Inspector differs from the typed SPL
rules.name: Search calls macros the critic cannot see inside
rules.risk_rationale: Not a defect — an audit-coverage gap. A clean verdict on a macro-heavy search is only as complete as the macros are benign.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Use | fields to trim columns mid-pipeline (distributable); reserve table for the final display stage.
rules.cost_rationale: table is transforming — it centralizes rows and drops fields mid-flight. Downstream commands then run on the SH against a format meant for display.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: pipeline stages after table all execute on the SH
rules.name: table in mid-pipeline
rules.risk_rationale: Dropped fields silently break downstream lookups/evals that expected them.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Match whole segments or use TERM() for exact tokens containing punctuation; split the filter into anchored parts.
rules.cost_rationale: Wildcards spanning punctuation (host=sh-*splunkcloud*) fight the segmenter: Splunk indexes segments split on punctuation, so matching costs more.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: unexpected result membership; elevated command.search.index
rules.name: Mid-token wildcard across punctuation
rules.risk_rationale: Correctness hazard, not just cost — segment boundaries mean mid-token wildcards can silently match differently than intended.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Set realtime_schedule=0 (continuous schedule) so missed windows are evaluated late rather than never; then fix the cause of the skips (self-overlap or scheduler pressure).
rules.cost_rationale: Cost is not the issue — coverage is. With realtime_schedule=1 (the default), a skipped run's time window is never evaluated at all.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scheduler log: status=skipped rows for this search while alert_actions configured
rules.name: Alert skipping evaluation windows
rules.risk_rationale: An alert with actions that has skipped runs has silent detection gaps: events in those windows were never inspected, and nothing tells the owner. The most dangerous failure mode a scheduled alert has.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Add | fields keep-list immediately after retrieval (fields is distributable streaming, so it runs on the indexers).
rules.cost_rationale: Without | fields, every extracted column ships indexers → SH for every surviving event, whether or not anything downstream uses it.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: dispatch.stream.remote bytes shrink when fields is added
rules.name: No early field trimming
rules.risk_rationale: None — pure bandwidth/memory overhead.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Add sourcetype= (and source=/host= where meaningful) to the retrieval stage.
rules.cost_rationale: An index filter alone pulls every event class in that index; sourcetype narrows the lexicon walk and downstream field extraction.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: eventCount well above what the target sourcetype alone would return
rules.name: Index without sourcetype scope
rules.risk_rationale: Extra event classes can also skew results (fields with the same name across sourcetypes).

rules.canonical_rewrite: Wrap exact punctuated tokens in TERM(): TERM(10.0.0.1), TERM(user@host).
rules.cost_rationale: High-cardinality exact tokens containing minor segmenters (IPs, GUIDs) match faster as TERM(10.0.0.1) — one lexicon term instead of a segment intersection.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.search.index drops when TERM() is applied to the same search
rules.name: Exact token without TERM()
rules.risk_rationale: Low risk; purely an efficiency opportunity.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Combine into one rex with multiple named groups, or promote stable extractions into props.conf/transforms.conf.
rules.cost_rationale: Each rex re-reads the source field per event; several in sequence multiply parse passes that one combined pattern (or props-based extraction) would do once.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.rex appears repeatedly in phase timings
rules.name: Sequential rex commands
rules.risk_rationale: Low — cost only.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Drop unused fields (especially _raw) before expanding: `... | fields - _raw | mvexpand <field>`, so the chunk stays under the cap.
rules.cost_rationale: mvexpand holds the entire expanded chunk in search-head memory; carrying _raw along multiplies the footprint per output row.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: 'mvexpand output will be truncated' warning in search.log
rules.name: mvexpand truncates at the memory cap
rules.risk_rationale: On overflow of max_mem_usage_mb (default 500 MB) mvexpand TRUNCATES the chunk and emits only a warning — the search succeeds with missing rows.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Use the documented indexed field for the sourcetype (props.conf / CIM), or add an indexed term alongside the extracted-field filter.
rules.cost_rationale: When an indexed (or default) field exists, filtering on the search-time equivalent forces _raw reads and extraction across more buckets.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: high command.search.kv relative to command.search.index
rules.name: Filtering on non-indexed form of an indexed field
rules.risk_rationale: Low correctness risk; cost and latency only.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Parenthesize: index=x (NOT *pattern*) — or better, replace the negation with an inclusion filter.
rules.cost_rationale: Minor cost impact; this is primarily a correctness trap.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: result set differs from the parenthesized form of the same search
rules.name: Unparenthesized NOT *
rules.risk_rationale: NOT * combined with index= or other filters without parentheses evaluates with surprising precedence — wrong results, no error.

rules.canonical_rewrite: For reports that tolerate flexible timing: schedule_window=auto and/or allow_skew=5m; reserve exact-time slots for searches that need them.
rules.cost_rationale: Non-alert reports that demand exact-time execution (allow_skew=0, no schedule_window) pile onto the same minute slots and crowd the scheduler — the thundering-herd ingredient.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: minute-slot histogram peak vs scheduler concurrency limit
rules.name: Frequent search without skew or schedule window
rules.risk_rationale: Contention it causes skips OTHER searches, including alerts.

rules.canonical_rewrite: For large or often-updated tables, write to a KV Store collection instead of a CSV (not bundle-replicated by default); keep CSV lookups small and rarely written; consider `override_if_empty=false` to avoid clobbering.
rules.cost_rationale: A CSV lookup table lives on the search head and is replicated to every indexer inside the knowledge bundle — and by default the whole table is re-sent each time any part of it changes. A large or frequently-written CSV bloats every search's bundle replication. (A KV Store target avoids this.)
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: bundle replication size/elapsed grows after the CSV is written
rules.name: outputlookup writes a bundle-replicated CSV
rules.risk_rationale: outputlookup is a flagged risky command (it can overwrite or lose data). Advisory: the CSV size is not visible in the SPL text, so this never blocks — most outputlookups are small and fine.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Fix the search structure (see its SPL findings — usually missing indexed filters, leading wildcards, or raw-data scans that tstats would answer); the window itself is fine, the search is slow for its size.
rules.cost_rationale: The search spends more wall-clock running than the span of data it examines — e.g. it reads 5 minutes of events but takes 10 minutes to finish. A pure inefficiency signal: the work is dominated by how the search is written, not by how much time it covers.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scheduler run_time vs (latest-earliest) dispatch span
rules.name: Runtime exceeds the time span searched
rules.risk_rationale: Runtime longer than the window makes self-overlap likely on any frequent schedule and wastes a scheduler slot for the whole duration.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Filter first: push search/where clauses before the transform; aggregate the smallest set that answers the question.
rules.cost_rationale: stats/sort/dedup are barriers: every event produced so far must arrive before they emit a row. Transforming the full candidate set then filtering the output wastes the whole difference.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: eventCount into the transform far exceeds rows out
rules.name: Transforming command before adequate filtering
rules.risk_rationale: Barrier commands lengthen runDuration — scheduled searches drift toward self-overlap.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Use historical relative-time bounds sized to the schedule (e.g. a */5 cron with earliest=-6m@m latest=now). If you truly need sub-second latency, an accelerated data model or an ingest-time pipeline scales where a standing real-time search does not.
rules.cost_rationale: A real-time dispatch window (rt- earliest / rt latest) runs a continuous search that holds a dedicated pipeline for as long as it lives — far more expensive than a periodic historical search, and it draws against the separate real-time search quota.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: dispatch.earliest_time/latest_time begins with rt; real-time search count in the scheduler
rules.name: Real-time dispatch on a scheduled search
rules.risk_rationale: "Scheduled" and "real-time" are contradictory intents: the search either runs continuously (pinning a slot the cron never releases) or its rt window is meaningless for a periodic run. Almost always a habit carried over from ad-hoc real-time searches, not a deliberate choice.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Make the search faster (see its SPL findings) or widen the interval to comfortably exceed p95 runtime.
rules.cost_rationale: Average runtime longer than the cron interval means every run collides with the next — the search occupies its slot continuously.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scheduler avg run_time vs cron interval; skip reason cites max_concurrent
rules.name: Runtime exceeds schedule interval
rules.risk_rationale: Guaranteed per-search max_concurrent skips: the schedule silently degrades to "whenever the previous run finishes".

rules.canonical_rewrite: Eliminate the pattern that can truncate (see JOIN_OVERUSE / SUBSEARCH_RISK rewrites); where a cap is genuinely acceptable, assert it explicitly with head and document why.
rules.cost_rationale: The cost is mostly already paid — this code is about the answer being wrong.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: 'truncating to maxout' messages in search.log
rules.name: Result set silently truncated
rules.risk_rationale: Truncation at subsearch_maxout / maxresultrows produces confidently wrong results. In an alerting search this means missed detections, not slowness.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Replace the pair with stats aggregation by the transaction key; if transaction is genuinely required, let it consume index order directly.
rules.cost_rationale: sort is a full-dataset barrier stacked in front of the already-expensive transaction — two SH-bound buffering passes back to back.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: two consecutive SH-phase spikes (sort buffer, then transaction assembly)
rules.name: sort immediately before transaction
rules.risk_rationale: Usually a symptom: the author is fighting transaction's ordering requirement, a strong smell that stats is the right tool.

rules.canonical_rewrite: State the bound: `sort 0 <field>` keeps everything (accepting the memory cost), `sort <N> <field>` takes an explicit top-N. Never rely on the implicit 10,000 default.
rules.cost_rationale: sort is a full-dataset barrier on the search head — the whole set is buffered before anything is emitted.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: result count pinned at exactly 10000 at the sort stage
rules.name: Unbounded sort truncates at 10,000
rules.risk_rationale: A sort with no explicit count defaults to 10,000 results and silently discards the rest BEFORE downstream commands see them — a top-N over a larger set is computed on the wrong 10k, with no error. Harmless under 10k rows, wrong above it.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Decide whether the search matters. If it does, raise schedule_priority or move it off the contended minute (schedule_window=auto / allow_skew) so it stops colliding with the herd. If it does not, disable it. Either way, stop paying for a schedule that mostly never runs.
rules.cost_rationale: The waste is inverted: a starved search barely consumes I/O because it is mostly being skipped. You are paying for a detection or report that rarely executes, and the slots it does win are spent losing races against the herd.
rules.doc_citation: Configure the priority of scheduled reports — https://help.splunk.com/en/?resourceId=Splunk_Report_Configurethepriorityofscheduledreports
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scheduler status=skipped ratio with reason citing concurrency; schedule_priority=default
rules.name: Chronically skipped at default priority
rules.risk_rationale: Skipped far more often than it runs, due to scheduler contention rather than its own runtime, while sitting at default priority — so nothing will change: it keeps losing the slot lottery. Its alerts and reports silently do not fire, yet the search still looks enabled and healthy in the list.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Restructure as a single search with a join key (stats by), a lookup, or a subsearch that feeds terms into one outer search.
rules.cost_rationale: map dispatches one search per input row (default cap 10). Raising maxsearches turns one query into a concurrent search storm competing for scheduler slots.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: spawned search count in _audit; scheduler skip events while running
rules.name: map with high maxsearches
rules.risk_rationale: Concurrency pressure skips OTHER searches — the blast radius is the whole scheduler, not this search.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Keep subsearches small and bounded (indexed filters, tight window); for large ID sets use lookups; for correlation use stats over a combined base search.
rules.cost_rationale: Every subsearch is a full extra search dispatched before the outer one can proceed; the outer search blocks on it.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: subsearch runtime near 60s or result count at exactly 10000 in search.log
rules.name: Subsearch nearing platform caps
rules.risk_rationale: Defaults: 60s timeout (subsearch_maxtime), 10k results (subsearch_maxout). Hitting either finalizes the subsearch early and the outer search runs on partial input — silently.

rules.canonical_rewrite: stats earliest(_time) AS start latest(_time) AS end values(...) BY id — add range(_time) for duration; reserve transaction for genuine startswith/endswith session semantics.
rules.cost_rationale: transaction is centralized streaming: every candidate event is held in SH memory while transactions assemble. It also requires descending time order, defeating index-order streaming.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: SH memory growth; eviction warnings in search.log; eventCount >> resultCount at the transaction stage
rules.name: transaction at scale
rules.risk_rationale: At maxopentxn (5000) / maxopenevents (100k) Splunk evicts LRU transactions — results are silently incomplete. Docs and community agree: >90% of transaction uses are better served by stats.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Constrain inside where: | tstats count from datamodel=Network_Traffic where nodename=All_Traffic index=fw by All_Traffic.action.
rules.cost_rationale: tstats over an accelerated data model without index/sourcetype constraints scans all summary buckets — bloom-filter bucket elimination does not apply to DMA summaries the way it does to raw buckets.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: summary bucket scan counts across all indexes feeding the model
rules.name: tstats/datamodel without index scope
rules.risk_rationale: "It uses tstats so it is fast" is a false comfort at portfolio scale; these grow with the summary footprint.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Filter on model/indexed fields inside tstats; apply lookup enrichment and lookup-based filters after the tstats aggregation.
rules.cost_rationale: A where clause that can only be satisfied via an automatic lookup forces the full lookup to load and apply during what should be a tsidx-only operation.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.search.lookups phase time inside a tstats search
rules.name: Expensive automatic lookup inside tstats where
rules.risk_rationale: Cost only, but it silently converts the fast path into a slow one.

rules.canonical_rewrite: | tstats count where index=web by host — instead of index=web | stats count by host.
rules.cost_rationale: Aggregating only indexed fields (index, sourcetype, source, host, _time) through raw-event stats reads _raw for nothing. tstats answers from tsidx alone — routinely 10-100x faster.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: A/B runDuration stats vs tstats form
rules.name: stats where tstats would serve
rules.risk_rationale: None — opportunity, not hazard. (Semantics differ slightly: tstats counts from tsidx; validate parity when converting.)

rules.canonical_rewrite: Name the indexes that actually hold the data: index=web OR index=app. If the index is unknown, find it once with | eventcount summarize=false index=* or metadata, then pin it.
rules.cost_rationale: index=* scans every index: metadata explosion plus I/O across all buckets. Splunk treats it as a literal instruction to search everything, not a convenience default.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scanCount orders of magnitude above resultCount; command.search.index dominates phase timings
rules.name: Unbounded index scan (index=*)
rules.risk_rationale: Competes with every other search for IOPS and scheduler slots; on shared infrastructure a single index=* over a wide window can starve the cluster.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Run reporting searches in smart or fast mode; verbose is for interactive exploration.
rules.cost_rationale: Verbose mode extracts and returns every field and event even when the search only needs aggregates — pure overhead for reporting searches.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: command.search.kv cost with no downstream field consumers
rules.name: Verbose search mode where smart/fast suffices
rules.risk_rationale: None — cost only.

rules.canonical_rewrite: Size the window to the interval plus a small safety overlap (e.g. */5 cron with earliest=-6m@m); for rolling aggregates use summary indexing instead of re-scanning history every run.
rules.cost_rationale: A search that runs every 5 minutes over 24 hours of events re-scans the same data ~288 times a day — the window/interval ratio is a direct I/O multiplier on every run.
rules.job_inspector_confirmation: scanCount per run vs new events per interval; scheduler runDuration vs cron period
rules.name: Dispatch window far exceeds schedule interval
rules.risk_rationale: Oversized windows push runDuration toward the cron interval (self-overlap skips) and usually signal copy-pasted dispatch settings nobody reviewed.

verdict_policy.description: The single, unified verdict policy: how the worst finding severity maps to a verdict. block_at/warn_at are minimum severities in the order below. One honest verdict — critique is not a per-role dial; enforcement is a separate concern.
